q: What is the carbon footprint of zinc oxide per tonne?
title: Zinc oxide per tonne
short: Most zinc oxide in India is made by vaporising zinc metal or zinc ash in a furnace and oxidising the vapour. The fuel or electricity for the furnace is the plant's own share. The zinc metal bought in carries the larger upstream footprint from smelting.

ul: Scope 1: furnace fuel, often furnace oil or gas.
Scope 2: electricity for fans and bagging.
Scope 3: zinc metal or zinc ash bought in.

p: Zinc oxide is not among CBAM goods, but EU tyre and ceramic buyers may still ask for a figure for their own reporting.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
